findings.evidence: Lines 123-132: the only uses of `hspace` and `hv` are building `w := Sum.elim (fun _ => 0) fun i => v (Sum.inr i)` and `hspace w hw`; the final `exact` calls `eqOn_of_eqOn_euclideanSection hf hg hUo hU ⟨_, hspace w hw, hwE⟩ hfg`, whose statement (line 97) already yields `EqOn f g U` from the weaker nonemptiness hypothesis.
findings.fix: Move the spacelike content into the conclusion, so `hspace` is genuinely used and the witness disappears: hypotheses `hf hg hUo hU hspace hfg`, conclusion `∀ v : Vector d, causalCharacter v = .spaceLike → f (ofMinkowski v) = g (ofMinkowski v)` — for each such `v`, its own equal-time projection supplies the nonempty intersection, and `hspace v hv` lands the point in `U`. This is also the acceptance-example wording the PR description claims for this theorem. If `EqOn f g U` is also wanted, get it from `eqOn_of_eqOn_euclideanSection` with the single membership `ofMinkowski w ∈ U`.
findings.issue: `hspace : ∀ v, causalCharacter v = .spaceLike → ofMinkowski v ∈ U` is far stronger than the proof needs — it is applied only once, at the equal-time projection `w` (line 132, `hspace w hw`) — and the conclusion `EqOn f g U` is exactly the conclusion of `eqOn_of_eqOn_euclideanSection` (line 97), which needs only `(U ∩ euclideanSection d).Nonempty`. A domain that contains the equal-time spacelike slice but not every spacelike vector (the generic case before a Jost-type theorem) cannot use this statement even though the conclusion holds for it. The implicit witness `{v} (hv : causalCharacter v = .spaceLike)` exists solely to feed `hspace`.

summary: The Mathematics-level identity theorem sits at the right level and its assumptions are all used. `eqOn_of_eqOn_euclideanSection_of_spaceLike` carries a ∀-quantified hypothesis that its proof uses at a single point while its conclusion is literally that of the weaker `eqOn_of_eqOn_euclideanSection`.
